fullAnalysis: Aromatherapy, Unscented, and Votive do not immediately suggest one clean category, so the board feels broader than it really is at the start. That is why a broad early read like "Party supplies" can feel plausible before the category becomes specific enough to trust. The clue that changes the frame is "Votive".

From there, reading them as candles explains the board cleanly. Entries like Aromatherapy, Unscented, and Votive stop feeling miscellaneous and start reading like parts of one tight set. Once votive makes the category specific enough to trust, the earlier clues stop feeling miscellaneous and start pulling toward the same shelf. The clues cover a range of uses, from practical to celebratory, which obscures the underlying product category.

I did not have a clean read from the first clue. Aromatherapy and Unscented still left room for Gifts, so that was the first direction I tested. That idea held for a moment, but it never explained Votive cleanly enough.

The turn came when I stopped treating votive as just another item and asked what kind of candle each clue described. Once that clue made the frame specific enough to trust, I went back through the board and checked whether each clue belonged on the same shelf. Entries like Aromatherapy and Unscented stopped feeling miscellaneous and started behaving like one clean set, which was when the solve clicked.
